_readme: TWO PASSES, IN ORDER. Pass 1 is `inventory` — what is this source even about.
Pass 2 is `dimensions` — is it good enough to build from. Do not start pass 2 until
every inventory row is filled: a grade over a corpus you have not identified is a
grade of your own assumptions.
INVENTORY (pass 1), one row per file — EVERY file under sourceRoot, no format skipped —
filled by OPENING it:
kind:        docs | code | data | ui | contract | unknown
answers:     which dimension keys this source can speak to, e.g. ["domain","rules"].
Empty list is a real answer — say so rather than leaving it null.
statedScope: if the source declares its own boundary, quote it VERBATIM. Sources
that say what they do not cover are the cheapest scope signal there is.
components:  named modules/components/aggregates this source defines, one string each.
format/route/media/pages are stamped by init from bin/lib/source-formats.tsv — what the
file is by extension, the extraction route that consumes it whole, and how
many embedded images/diagrams a text-only read would leave behind. A row
with media > 0 is not consumed until its disposition accounts for them.
DISPOSITIONS (Stage 1) — one entry per inventory row (or a glob covering several), read
by bin/source-ledger.sh, which blocks the Stage 1 and 2 gates while any row has none:
{"path": "<rel>" | "pattern": "<glob over rel>", "state": "extracted",
"artifact": "<project-relative file or dir that carries what was extracted>",
"evidence": "<one specific finding that came OUT of the file, and where it landed>",
"media": <images described, must equal the row's media count, or "mediaWaived": "why">,
"by": "who", "date": "YYYY-MM-DD"}
The artifact must exist, be non-empty, and NAME the source file — a disposition that
says 'the triage already used it' is checked by grepping the triage for the file, and
fails if it never mentions it. Write them with: bin/source-ledger.sh mark ...
A file deliberately not extracted is a register line, not a disposition:
bin/gate-check.sh <project> --waive source/<rel> --reason "..."
DIMENSIONS (pass 2). Fill in every dimension by READING the sources. Do not infer a
rating from file size.
rating: absent | named | specified | verified
evidence: where you saw it (page, section, screen) — or why you concluded absent.
consequence: what the BUILD has to invent if this stays as-is. Be concrete.
Leave rating null for any dimension you did not actually check; the report will
refuse to score rather than treat unchecked as absent.

dispositions.evidence: documents-index.md lists every basename under sources/ (36 pages, 4 markdown, 38 images, 122 chrome files); content read finding: ch09's fig-booking-form-validation.png is the only place 'IMO number must be exactly 7 digits' is stated -> source-sufficiency.json conflict C3

actors.demands: Who uses the system, and where one role's authority stops
actors.evidence: roles.md + ch05 (05-stakeholders-and-roles.html): four named roles (Shipping Agent, Berth Officer, Harbour Master, Inspector), one role per user, role shown in every screen header; Harbour Master's extra powers over Berth Officer are named explicitly.
actors.consequence: None — build the four roles as given.

domain.demands: Entities, their attributes, and the relationships between them
domain.evidence: ch07/12/14/18/20/26/36 + glossary.md: 11 entities with attribute name, type, length and required/optional for every field, plus an explicit relationships list (ch07, ch12, ch36).
domain.consequence: None — the domain model in the thin BRDs is close to a direct transcription.

processes.demands: Flows and sequences: what happens after what, and what state it leaves behind
processes.evidence: ch08 (status model Draft..Completed, fast-track rule, submission timing), ch11 (onboarding/suspension), ch15/16 (review + decision outcomes), ch22-25 (inspection -> departure clearance).
processes.consequence: None — sequences and the state each leaves behind are stated.

rules.demands: Business rules, validations, thresholds, calculations, eligibility criteria
rules.evidence: Concrete thresholds throughout: 30-day max stay, 90-day/48h submission window, 120m fast-track LOA, 0.5m draught clearance, 15% late-arrival surcharge (>2h), 80m waiver threshold, 50% late-cancellation fee, 21% VAT, 250/day shore power, High-severity->Failed inspection rule, 3-overdue-invoices auto-suspend. Two of these (IMO exactly-7-digits, rejection-reason-required) exist ONLY in prototype screenshots, not in any chapter's text — see conflicts.
rules.consequence: None for the stated rules; the two image-only rules and the two conflicts below need a decision.

ui.demands: Screens, navigation, layout, and which data appears on which
ui.evidence: ch28-32 name the screen set and per-screen behaviour (filters, drag-drop, own-requests-only); three prototype screenshots (ch08, ch09, ch21) show exact field labels, a validation message style (red inline text) and the left-nav item list.
ui.consequence: Only 3 of 8 named screens have a screenshot; the rest are wireframed from prose in Stage 3.

integrations.demands: External systems, protocols, credentials, and behaviour when they fail
integrations.evidence: ch33: one integration named (AIS position feed), with a poll interval (5 minutes) and a trigger behaviour (flag Arrived on geofence entry) but no protocol, endpoint, auth, or failure-mode.
integrations.consequence: Build will have to invent or stub the AIS connector's transport/auth/failure handling; recommend Stage 3 records it as a stub integration pending a real contract.

nfr.demands: Security, performance, availability, retention, data volumes
nfr.evidence: ch26 (audit trail on every status change), ch27 (one preference cookie, no analytics), ch35 (company-scoped visibility) touch security/audit/privacy but no chapter states a performance, availability, retention or data-volume target.
nfr.consequence: No load/uptime/retention numbers exist anywhere in the corpus; Stage 3 NFR question has nothing to inherit and must ask the user directly rather than 'confirm what's in the source'.

tenancy.demands: Whether one deployment serves many organisations, and how their data is isolated
tenancy.evidence: No chapter or workshop note mentions more than one port authority or more than one deployment; ch35's company-level visibility rule is row-level security within a single deployment, not multi-tenant SaaS (tracked instead under security_model).
tenancy.consequence: Assume single-tenant, one port authority, unless the user says otherwise at Stage 3.

security_model.demands: The actor-to-permission mapping: who may do each thing, and who may not
security_model.evidence: roles.md + ch05: 4 roles, explicit permission deltas (Harbour Master = Berth Officer + overrides + reactivation + tariff maintenance); ch13 (surcharge waiver = Harbour Master only); ch16 (override = Harbour Master only); ch35 (agents see only their own company's data).
security_model.consequence: None — enough to build role-based access + one row-security rule for Stage 3/4.

data_migration.demands: Existing data, its volume and shape, and how cutover happens
data_migration.evidence: ADR-003 (decisions-log.md) states all example data is invented; no chapter mentions existing records, volumes, or a cutover; this is a docs-only corpus with no legacy system behind it.
data_migration.consequence: No migration/cutover — Stage 4/7 build only needs Stage 5 demo/seed data, never a data migration.

conflicts.text: Cancellation-fee windows overlap and disagree: ch10 (06-cancellation-and-changes) says cancellation is 'free of charge until 24 hours before ETA'; ch19 (tariffs-cancellation-fees) says 'cancellations made within 72 hours of ETA are charged 50% of the berth fee'. Between 72h and 24h before ETA the two rules contradict (free, per ch10, vs 50%, per ch19).

Navigation count disagrees with the prototype: ch28 (navigation-and-screens) states 'the navigation offers three screens: Booking Board, My Bookings and Inspection Calendar'; the prototype screenshots embedded in ch08/ch09/ch21 all show a five-item left nav — Booking Board, My Bookings, Inspections, Tariffs, Reports.

IMO number length rule disagrees between the domain tables and the prototype: ch07/ch14 domain tables say IMONumber is 'Text, up to 7 characters' (i.e. 0-7); the booking-form validation screenshot (ch09) says 'IMO NUMBER MUST BE EXACTLY 7 DIGITS' (exactly 7, numeric). The exact-length, numeric-only rule exists ONLY in the image.

ApprovalDecision.Reason is 'Optional' in the data dictionary (ch36), but the officer review screen screenshot (ch21) shows a conditional-required validation: 'REJECTION REASON IS REQUIRED WHEN OUTCOME IS REJECTED'. Not a hard contradiction (the field can stay optional and be conditionally required by a rule) but the conditional rule exists ONLY in the image and must be modelled explicitly, not inferred from 'Optional'.

choices.text: Cargo-manifest attachment: workshop-notes.md session 2 says 'Agents must be able to attach the cargo manifest as a PDF to a booking request', with the size limit explicitly 'not decided'. No chapter (incl. ch07 domain overview, ch09 booking form) gives BookingRequest a file/attachment relationship at all. This is a shape-changing gap — it adds a new relationship/entity, not just a detail.

Workshop-notes.md session 3: 'The review screen must show the last five bookings of the same vessel.' Not present in ch15 (officer-review-process) or ch21 (officer-review-screen), which describe the review screen without this cross-booking panel. Shape-changing: needs a bounded reverse-lookup query on the review screen wireframe.

Workshop-notes.md session 2: agents 'want the e-mail notifications to include the reference'. ch17 (notifications) only says 'the agent receives an e-mail whenever the status of their booking request changes', with no stated content. Minor but still a silence on notification content that a build would otherwise invent.

notes: Docs-ready corpus (36 HTML pages + 4 markdown files, saved-webpage export). Converted once via bin/html-to-md.sh; every page and markdown file plus every embedded image was opened. Two prototype screenshots and one form-validation figure carry rules found nowhere in the prose (see conflicts C3/C4); the other 36 per-page images are captioned stock photography ('Container terminal at dawn') and carry no functional content. See conflicts (C1-C4) and choices (S1-S3) above for what Stage 0's scope brainstorm must put to the user.
